clue.text: Pat, say, felt to be useless in the field

parts.note: a pat is a small slab of butter, so 'say' marks an example
felt in the sense of touched or handled, i.e. fingered

explanation.surface: Someone called Pat is judged a hopeless fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a person's name; it is a pat of butter. In cricket, a fielder who drops catches is said to be butterfingered.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy fielders who keep dropping the ball are described with this word.

clue.text: His produce is cut (yet dear in France)

parts.note: yet as a conjunction means but
the French word for dear is cher

explanation.surface: A tradesman whose goods are sliced, though costly across the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat trader sells joints and chops, produce that is cut up.

clue.text: Battle area for soldiers has a column in it

parts.note: the Battle of Trafalgar, Nelson's naval victory of 1805
a square is a parade ground, or a formation of troops

explanation.surface: A military site with a pillar standing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAFALGAR SQUARE is the London square where Nelson's Column stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The London landmark is famous for Nelson's monument pillar at its centre.

clue.text: Dash from the land

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone sprints away from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'the' and the start of 'land'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of verve or flair is a synonym.

clue.text: Iron rule of Leo, for example

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a rule is a ruled line

explanation.surface: A strict regime under a lion's star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is the lion, and lions are cats, so of Leo means catlike.

clue.text: Ancient craft of patriarch on Channel Island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: Noah is one of the Old Testament patriarchs
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: An old boat belonging to a patriarch is moored off a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the answer comes from 'of patriarch' read as patriarch's; Sark lies between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel built for the Flood is a very old boat.

clue.text: Fan it as the sun comes out

indicators.note: comes out suggests the letters emerging in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wave a fan as the sun breaks through.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is a keen supporter or devotee.

clue.text: It is in print, for crying out loud!

definitions.text: It is in print, for crying out loud!

parts.words: It is in print, for crying out loud!
parts.note: the punctuation mark used in writing to show shouting or exclamation, and the clue ends on one

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about something appearing in print.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed stroke-and-dot shows an outcry or emphatic remark.

clue.text: Respectable little church in the hollow

indicators.note: in places the church inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow
CE is short for Church of England

explanation.surface: A worthy small chapel in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means proper and morally acceptable.

clue.text: To chase around Virginia is very hard work

indicators.note: around puts the chase word around the state's abbreviation

parts.note: to trail is to follow or chase
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Pursuing someone all over Virginia is exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is laborious toil.

clue.text: Object of broadcast recital

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: The point of a recital going out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a thing or item.

clue.text: Try to listen!

definitions.meaning: a judge tries a case, i.e. sits to judge it in court
the command to attend with the ears

explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case when trying it, and hearing means listening.

clue.text: Join closely at home-and kiss

parts.note: in means at home
to osculate is to kiss

explanation.surface: Get close at home and kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Inosculate means to unite closely, as blood vessels do.

clue.text: Job for a top-drawer sort only, it is presumed?

definitions.text: Job for a top-drawer sort only, it is presumed?

parts.words: Job for a top-drawer sort only, it is presumed?
parts.note: top-drawer seems to mean upper-class but here means the best at drawing a weapon

explanation.surface: Some posts are presumed open only to the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: Top-drawer usually means posh; here it is someone quickest at drawing a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wild West gunfighter needs to be the fastest on the draw.

clue.text: This course can be fun for students abroad

parts.note: rag is the British name for students' charity fundraising fun and pranks
abroad in the sense of out and about

explanation.surface: A course of study offering fun for students overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Course means a dish in a meal, not a study programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a stew served as part of a meal.

clue.text: At craft, I could produce one

definitions.text: At craft, I could produce one

indicators.note: could produce suggests these letters being remade into a new word

explanation.surface: With skill, I could make one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could produce' rearranges ATCRAFTI, and the whole clue describes an object made by human skill.
explanation.definitionFit: An object made with craft is a man-made object of this kind.

clue.text: Bitter, possibly, about desert puzzle

indicators.note: about puts the drink around the wasteland word

parts.note: bitter is a kind of beer
a wild is a desert or wilderness

explanation.surface: A pint of bitter in the desert would be baffling.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle someone is to confuse them.

clue.text: Capital he's taking for church districts

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A capital takes over church districts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastical units served by one priest.

clue.text: The insurance contract that makes good sense?

definitions.meaning: the document setting out an insurance cover
a sensible course of action, as in honesty is the best one

explanation.definitionFit: An insurer issues this document, and the word also means a prudent plan of action.

clue.text: Court of Anglo-Saxon dimensions

parts.note: size means dimensions

explanation.surface: A court with Anglo-Saxon proportions.
explanation.walkthrough: The assizes were periodic courts held in English counties until 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: An assize was a travelling judicial session.

clue.text: There is only one such character in Delos

definitions.text: There is only one such character in Delos

parts.words: There is only one such character in Delos
parts.note: Delos is a Greek island, and its name contains a single letter E, whose Greek counterpart is the letter meant

explanation.surface: A Greek island has only one such inhabitant.
explanation.walkthrough: Character looks like a person but is a letter: DELOS has one E, the Greek letter of that sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth Greek letter corresponds to E.

clue.text: Soldiers finish meal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
past in the sense of over or finished

explanation.surface: Soldiers clear their plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the formal word for a spread of food eaten at one sitting.

clue.text: £51 rise, perhaps, should get one a kitchen-appliance

parts.note: 51 in Roman numerals is LI, and a pound is a quid, so £51 gives LI and QUID

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A pay rise of fifty-one pounds should buy a new gadget for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RISE into ISER. Quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A blender that purees food is this kitchen device.

clue.text: Star-ring, going the wrong way, could become a burden

indicators.note: going the wrong way says the pair is read from right to left

parts.note: the sun is a star
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A celebrity's ring, misused, becomes a burden.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, SUNO gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus is a duty or responsibility.

clue.text: Two enlisted guys in musical show

indicators.note: two means the piece is used twice

parts.note: GI is a US enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: Two soldiers appear in a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a stage and film musical by Lerner and Loewe.

clue.text: Asked a price for having produced power

definitions.meaning: filled with electricity, like a battery

explanation.definitionFit: The word means billed for goods, and also holding an electric current.

clue.text: A large beer called for the lady's-maid

indicators.note: called for means spoken aloud, so the order is a homophone

parts.note: a big ale, run together

explanation.surface: Someone orders a large beer for the lady's maid.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old literary word for a lady's maid, from a character in a 17th-century play.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a female personal servant.

clue.text: Sort of square slips delude England's openers, really in awe

parts.note: a T-square is a kind of square used in drawing
slips are errors
to trick is to delude
the opening two letters of England

explanation.surface: A cricket report: square-leg fumbles and slips cost England's opening batsmen dearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Square and slips look like cricket fielding positions; they are T and ERRORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror-stricken means overwhelmed with fear, far beyond mere awe.
